lesson_title: The Highlights Reel and the Team Photo: Partnership Financial Statements
hook_text: One statement is a movie. The other is a photo. Confuse them and the marks walk away.
clip_script: When a rugby season ends, two things get made. The highlights reel — everything that happened from the first whistle to the last. And the squad photo — everyone lined up on the final day. Nobody asks the photo what the halftime score was in May. That is exactly the two financial statements. The Statement of Comprehensive Income is the reel: FOR the year ended, the whole earning story — sales of R2 880 000 in the opening scene, costs cut away shot by shot, net profit of R528 000 in the final frame. The Statement of Financial Position is the photo: ON 28 February, one frozen day — everything the business owns on one side, everyone with a claim on the other. And the photo rule: both rows must stand equally tall. R1 175 400 owned, R1 175 400 claimed. Every time. Why keep both? Because each is blind where the other sees. The reel cannot tell you if next month's accounts can be paid. The photo cannot tell you if the year went well. And beneath every big number sits a note — the fine print with the workings — climbing to the exact figure on the face. Face for the conclusion. Note for the proof.
visual_style: A split frame: film reel spooling through the year's income lines on one side, a formal squad photo assembling asset by asset on the other; two towers rising to identical heights, ledger-paper textures with school-sport colours.
pacing: Rolling montage for the reel, a sharp freeze for the photo, then a slow tower-balance reveal.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and build both statements to the last balancing rand.
